title: Edge aggregator + adaptive windowing to reduce console metrics cardinality and backend load
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight edge-side aggregation layer that pre-aggregates high-frequency console metrics into adaptive time windows before they reach the core stream processors. Goal is to reduce downstream throughput/costs and smooth bursts while preserving the fidelity required for SLO alerting and per-route dashboards.
technical_decisions: Perform aggregation at the ingress sidecar (envoy filter) and at an intermediate Kafka topic named console.edge-aggregates
Use Flink streaming jobs to perform final windowing and enrichment; Flink state backend (RocksDB) for window state snapshots
Windowing style: hybrid approach — micro-windows (1s) with periodic compaction into adaptive windows (1s, 5s, 30s) based on metric volatility
Deterministic partitioning by (customer_id, route_id, metric_name) hash to keep aggregation idempotent and colocated
Sampling + suppression: for ultra-high-cardinality labels (e.g., dynamic request_id), apply label pruning and approximate counters (HyperLogLog) at edge to avoid cardinality explosion

Exactly-once writes are expensive; we will aim for at-least-once ingest with dedup by event_id and 5s watermarking in Flink. Downstream storage writes will be idempotent by key (time_bucket+partition+metric_key)
Schema: Avro with a top-level "type" field and versioned namespace; evolve using Confluent compatible registry. All events include event_id, ingest_ts, source_node, and provenance tags
Backpressure: edge sidecar will accept burst buffering with a bounded in-memory queue + disk spill and expose a circuit-breaker metric to Console so we can route traffic away from saturated pods
Operational metrics: pipeline will export per-customer aggregations ingested, percent of events suppressed, and aggregate compression ratio to Console metrics dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Downstream event count (to core topics) reduced by >= 60% for sample workload (internal playground traffic)
99th percentile ingest latency added by edge aggregator < 10ms under steady state; tail under burst < 200ms including disk spill
Per-route metric error vs raw-pipeline aggregate <= 0.5% for top 100 routes, and bounded for tail routes where approximate counters used
No customer-visible data loss in canary tests for 72h; dedup mechanism prevents duplicate increments after restarts
Automated rollback path validated: ability to disable aggregation flag and replay raw events to core topics without schema incompatibility
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit + integration tests, load tests against staging ingestion harness (target QPS 2x prod peak)
Phase 1 (Canary): route 1% of traffic from internal tenants; monitor compression ratio, error against raw pipeline, and sidecar circuit-breaker
Phase 2 (Scaled Canary): expand to 5% and 20% if SLOs met for 48h each; run end-to-end dashboards and alerting smoke tests
Phase 3: customer cohorts toggle (per-tenant opt-in) for critical customers for another 7 days
Phase 4: full roll when stability and telemetry thresholds are met; enable adaptive windowing globally
Fallback: persistent feature flag in control plane to revert to raw event forwarding; a replay tool will republish edge-aggregator deltas to core topics for backfill
comments: 2025-01-12 - Arielle Chen: Initial design sketch posted to Confluence; proposed adaptive windows to handle bursty developer console events.

2025-01-20 - Marcus Reed: Spike completed - implemented sidecar prototype that groups by (customer, route, metric) and emits micro-batches. Observed 4.3x reduction in staging throughput for common dashboards.
2025-01-27 - Review (SRE): raised concern about state store size on node restarts. Decided to persist checkpoint info to S3 and reduce in-memory retention to 60s for micro-windows.
2025-01-30 - Security review: confirmed Avro schema + registry meets our compliance requirements; no PII fields allowed in metrics payload. Marked as security_review_required=true

2025-02-02 - QA: load test with synthetic 10k TPS burst. Edge aggregator buffered and spilled to disk as expected; restored without duplicates after simulated pod kill using dedup token and Flink checkpointing. Minor follow-up: improve disk cleanup and metrics emission on spill events.

2025-02-04 - Marcus Reed: Began canary deployment for internal apps; initial 1% traffic shows expected compression and latency SLOs met. Will expand to 5% on 2025-02-06 pending no regressions. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-ingest/pull/412
